rows.name: AgentCourt (adversarial evolvable lawyer agents)
rows.families: adversarial litigation argumentation; lawyer-agent self-improvement via case experience; adversarial courtroom simulation (evolvable lawyer agents vs judge/plaintiff/defendant roles); post-evolution lawyer-skill evaluation (CourtBench)
rows.requires: Adversarial matter shape: two agent seats (our side / opposing counsel) attached to one matter, a scripted judge NPC, per-round debate transcripts persisted as matter documents, and a growing firm knowledge base the agent may write to — the self-evolution loop maps directly onto a firm world's precedent/playbook stores; grading needs lawyer-rubric LLM-judge plus win/loss outcome fields.
rows.proof: Needs multi-agent adversarial courtroom interaction and Chinese corpora; the world is single-agent, English.

rows.name: AgentsCourt / SimuCourt (+ Legal-KB)
rows.families: court debate simulation; precedent/statute retrieval; judgment drafting; multi-stage decision refinement; judicial decision-making from case materials (court debate simulation → precedent/legal retrieval → judgment drafting)
rows.requires: A courtroom module bolted onto the firm world: case-bundle documents per matter (indictment, statements, facts), a retrieval tool over a statute+precedent KB (JudicialKB analogue), multi-role scripted participants (prosecutor/defense as NPC agents), and grading that compares generated judgments to the real gold judgment on verdict match (deterministic) + reasoning quality (judge-graded); second-instance cases add an appeal-chain task shape.
rows.proof: Multi-party court-debate simulation (judge/opposing counsel agents) — no counterparty mechanics in the world.

rows.name: ALKiln (SuffolkLITLab/ALKiln)
rows.families: write Gherkin tests for an interview; diagnose/fix interview logic from failing tests; regression testing of form changes
rows.requires: This is directly hostable: a docassemble instance + ALKiln runner as world infrastructure; tasks = interview repo with seeded defects + failing/passing test oracle. Fully deterministic pass/fail grading with zero LLM judging — a rare executable-verifier anchor for legal workflow tasks.
rows.proof: Requires a guided-interview/form runtime plus a Gherkin test executor; the world has no interview engine.

rows.name: Crosby Multi-turn Negotiation Bench
rows.families: multi-turn contract negotiation; redline response; playbook adherence
rows.requires: A counterparty actor that issues redlines over multiple rounds, a negotiation playbook document with escalation thresholds, and a redline diff tool. Complements Harvey LAB's single-turn redline tasks with genuine multi-turn state; grading needs playbook-compliance checks (deterministic where thresholds are numeric).
rows.proof: Single-turn redline-vs-playbook adherence is hosted (deep-drafting tasks task_180–task_185 (6 tasks): counterparty markup reconciled against internal playbook, superseding-instruction compliance). The multi-turn bargaining loop with a live counterparty is not (no opposing agent).

rows.name: Harvey LAB extensions: M&A Due Diligence (+ announced enterprise search, fund formation, investigations/discovery)
rows.families: VDR due diligence review; diligence reporting
rows.requires: Extends the already-inventoried Harvey LAB: the firm world should plan for VDR-scale document stores (hundreds of files per matter) and diligence-report deliverables with per-issue rubric criteria — watch this repo for direct anchor tasks.
rows.proof: VDR-style diligence review hosted: harvey_lab diligence family (task_012, task_026, task_036…) — red-flags reporting over seeded deal folders with distractors — plus discovery-retrieval corpus tasks (task_186–task_193 (8 tasks)).

rows.name: OpenProBono
rows.families: cited legal research reports; source-verification (every claim cited); practice-area-scoped Q&A
rows.requires: A world needs a sealed legal-source corpus (statutes, cases, regs) exposed via search/retrieval tools plus a citation-graph table, so research tasks can be graded on (a) correct answer keys and (b) citation validity checked deterministically against the corpus — the OpenProBono bot architecture is the reference tool surface.
rows.proof: Evidence-grounded determinations with required full reads are hosted (discovery-retrieval tasks task_186–task_193 (8 tasks); hallucination-traps tasks task_194–task_200 (7 tasks) incl. a phantom-citation record). Open-web cited research reports are not (no live corpus); a citation-registry pack would close the cite-verification half.

rows.name: Ready Jurist One / J1Bench (J1-EVAL, FudanDISC)
rows.families: multi-participant procedural interaction; procedural-compliance execution; dynamic-environment legal tasks; interactive legal-intelligence tasks in dynamic multi-participant environments
rows.requires: Already the inventory's closest analogue: confirms the design pattern of procedural multi-participant environments with graded interaction; lawfirm-qwen's differentiator remains the executable filesystem/tool world and deterministic boundary-proven grading, which J1-EVAL lacks.
rows.proof: Multi-participant procedural interaction in Chinese — both mechanics absent.

rows.name: TERMS-Bench
rows.families: bilateral negotiation under private information
rows.requires: Not legal-specific, but the design pattern matters: give the counterparty a hidden reservation value and score the agent on computed surplus — a fully deterministic verifier for negotiation tasks the law-firm world could adopt for settlement/deal-term negotiation tasks.
rows.proof: Bilateral negotiation under private information requires an opposing agent.

rows.name: ACORD (Atticus Clause Retrieval Dataset)
rows.families: precedent clause retrieval for contract drafting
rows.requires: A clause-bank/precedent-library table (clause text, type, source agreement, quality rank) with a retrieval tool. Task shape maps directly to a firm world: 'pull the three best indemnification precedents from the firm knowledge base before drafting' — deterministic grading via gold rankings makes it one of the best verifiable sub-steps to embed inside a larger drafting task.
rows.proof: Closed by the acord-clause-retrieval pack (task_246–task_249 (4 tasks)): a 22-clause precedent library built on ACORD's real query taxonomy (governing law, LoL carve-outs, renewal-notice vs auto-renew, audit-rights thresholds) with withdrawn and counterparty-supplied distractors; selection is graded by pinned library slug.

rows.name: ArabLegalEval
rows.families: Arabic legal QA; translated legal reasoning
rows.requires: MCQ/QA tables; jurisdiction-expansion material with a synthetic-QA-from-regulations generation pipeline worth borrowing for authoring new firm-world tasks from any regulation set.
rows.proof: Arabic legal corpora; world is English-only.

rows.name: BSARD (Belgian Statutory Article Retrieval Dataset)
rows.families: statutory article retrieval; statutory article retrieval for citizen questions
rows.requires: French-language statute-research shape: statute table (article_id, code, text) with search tool; research tickets carrying a client question and gold article-ID sets; deterministic recall/precision grader; directly parallel to COLIEE Task 3 so one world 'statute research' task shape can host both EN/JA and FR instantiations.
rows.proof: French statutory corpus retrieval.

rows.name: CALRK-Bench
rows.families: context-grounded legal reasoning
rows.requires: Provided-context QA pairs with deterministic answers; a template for 'reason only from the matter file' tasks that punish parametric-knowledge shortcuts.
rows.proof: Korean legal corpora.

rows.name: CaseGen (multi-stage Chinese legal case document generation)
rows.families: drafting defense statements; writing trial facts; composing legal reasoning; generating judgment results
rows.requires: The closest published analogue to lawfirm-qwen's chained-matter shape: a matter lifecycle with 4 sequential deliverable slots, each stage consuming the prior stage's output as input documents; world needs per-stage reference documents and rubric-based LLM-judge grading, plus lifecycle state tracking so stage-N tasks unlock only after stage-N-1 filing — enables measuring error amplification like LegalWorld.
rows.proof: Chinese multi-stage judicial drafting corpus; language mechanic missing (the multi-stage drafting SHAPE exists in deep-drafting).

rows.name: Chinese Labor Law LLM Benchmark
rows.families: labor-law QA and case analysis (domain-vertical evaluation)
rows.requires: Evidence that practice-area verticals are benchmarkable: the world's employment-law department can host a labor-specific ticket family (dismissal-risk memos, severance computations with gold amounts, contract-clause compliance checks against a labor-statute table); computations graded numerically, citations by set match.
rows.proof: Chinese labor-law corpus.

rows.name: ContractEval
rows.families: clause-level risk identification; contract review; clause-level risk spotting; abstention calibration (no-clause detection)
rows.requires: Same substrate as CUAD (already in inventory) — full contract documents in a matter folder — but reframed for generative LLMs with the laziness metric. A firm world hosts it as 'review the counterparty draft and flag all 41 checklist risks'; verifier is span-overlap against gold, plus a penalty channel for omission, which is a good flakiness probe.
rows.proof: Clause-level risk identification with abstention calibration is exactly the cuad pack (task_157–task_166 (10 tasks)): per-category identification over executed contracts, absent-category fabrication traps graded as forbidden rows.

rows.name: DISC-Law-Eval (DISC-LawLLM evaluation suite)
rows.families: objective legal MCQ (single/multi answer, 3 difficulty bands); subjective legal QA graded by LLM judge
rows.requires: Same certification-exam shape as JEC-QA plus a client-consultation ticket shape: consultation tickets with reference answers and a rubric (accuracy/completeness/clarity) for LLM-judge grading; world needs a judge-prompt harness and reference-answer storage per ticket, alongside the deterministic MCQ table.
rows.proof: Chinese MCQ + LLM-judged subjective QA (language + judged-prose mechanics).

rows.name: DLawBench
rows.families: multi-turn consultation; fact elicitation
rows.requires: A simulated-client actor with a hidden fact sheet the agent must elicit — the tau-bench user-simulator pattern applied to legal intake. The firm world needs client personas with withheld facts and grading on whether the agent asked the right questions before advising.
rows.proof: Multi-turn client consultation dialogue in Chinese — no multi-turn client simulator.

rows.name: GerDaLIR (German Dataset for Legal Information Retrieval)
rows.families: legal information retrieval; extractive QA; subsumption reasoning; precedent retrieval (citation-derived relevance)
rows.requires: German-practice library: a large precedent table with full decision texts and a search tool; task shape = 'find the authority this draft passage should cite' — the agent gets a brief passage from a matter document and must return case IDs; deterministic recall@k grader against the gold citation set; large label volume makes it ideal for auto-generating many world tasks.
rows.proof: German retrieval corpora.

rows.name: Hallucination-detection cluster 2026 (Who Checks the Citations?; LegalHalluLens; Source or It Didn't Happen)
rows.families: citation hallucination detection; typed hallucination auditing
rows.requires: Gold authority tables (real vs fabricated citations with support labels). The firm world can inject fabricated authorities into matter files as canary probes and deterministically check whether agents catch or propagate them.
rows.proof: Abstention-under-absence is hosted with veto grading (hallucination-traps tasks task_194–task_200 (7 tasks), incl. phantom-citation and client-pressure documents). Typed citation-audit over long briefs is not; a cite-checking pack (seeded citation registry + defective briefs) would close it.

rows.name: IL-TUR (Indian Legal Text Understanding and Reasoning)
rows.families: classification; summarization; translation; extraction; retrieval; legal NER (L-NER); rhetorical role labeling of judgment sentences; court judgment prediction & explanation (via ILDC); bail prediction (Hindi, HLDC-based); legal statute identification; prior case retrieval; judgment summarization; cross-lingual tasks in 9 Indian languages
rows.requires: An India-desk bundle reusing existing shapes: NER→citation-index, rhetorical roles→'structure this judgment into facts/arguments/ruling sections' (sentence-label table with gold roles), bail prediction→intake-risk memo with gold binary column, statute ID→statute-table set match, PCR→precedent-retrieval with gold cited-case sets, summarization→reference-based grading; needs Hindi/Indic text support in the world's document store and graders.
rows.proof: Nine Indian languages + Indian court corpora.

rows.name: JBE-QA
rows.families: bar exam QA
rows.requires: MCQ table + exact-match grader; jurisdiction-expansion material only.
rows.proof: Japanese bar-exam corpus.

rows.name: JEC-QA (thunlp)
rows.families: judicial exam MCQ (knowledge-driven and case-analysis); knowledge-driven bar-exam MCQ; case-analysis bar-exam MCQ (with retrieval over legal materials)
rows.requires: Associate-certification task shape: a 'training/qualification' module in the firm world where agents must pass exam batches before unlocking matter work; needs a questions table (stem, options, gold answer set, KD/CA type tag) plus an optional legal-materials retrieval tool; grading is exact set-match on chosen options — fully deterministic and cheap.
rows.proof: Chinese judicial-exam corpus.

rows.name: KBL (Korean Benchmark for Legal Language Understanding)
rows.families: legal knowledge QA; legal reasoning; bar exam MCQ
rows.requires: MCQ bank + optional retrieval corpus; the open-book/closed-book toggle is the reusable design — the firm world can score every knowledge task both with and without its research tools to attribute performance to tooling.
rows.proof: Korean legal corpora.

rows.name: KoBLEX
rows.families: multi-hop statute QA
rows.requires: Statutes table with cross-reference links and multi-hop gold chains; the hop-chain gold pattern maps to the firm world's multi-step research tasks where intermediate lookups are verifiable (like LegalAgentBench's key_middle).
rows.proof: Korean multi-hop statute corpus.

rows.name: Korean Canonical Legal Benchmark
rows.families: knowledge-independent rule application
rows.requires: Self-contained rule+facts→conclusion items with exact answers; ideal deterministic filler tasks for the firm world that work in any jurisdiction because the rules ship with the task.
rows.proof: Korean corpora.

rows.name: LAiW (Chinese Legal LLM Benchmark)
rows.families: basic information retrieval (NER, article recommendation, element recognition); legal foundation inference (similar case matching, controversy focus mining, charge prediction); complex legal application (judgment prediction, judicial summarization, consultation)
rows.requires: A leveled task ladder in the world: tier-1 tasks (extract entities/elements from a filed document, recommend statute IDs), tier-2 (match precedents, identify dispute focus), tier-3 (draft judgment-prediction or consultation memos); world needs the same statute/precedent tables as CAIL shapes plus per-tier gold labels, and a progression rule that gates tier-3 matters on tier-1/2 pass rates — directly mirrors LAiW's claim that models skip basics.
rows.proof: Chinese legal-NLP corpus suite.

rows.name: LBox Open (Korean legal benchmark)
rows.families: case name classification from facts; statute prediction from facts; criminal judgment prediction (fine/imprisonment ranges); civil judgment prediction (claim acceptance level); precedent summarization
rows.requires: Korean-desk instantiation of the intake-assessment shape: matters with Korean fact narratives and gold columns (case_name, statute_ids[], sentence bucket, claim-acceptance ratio); statute lookup tool over Korean codes; summarization tasks graded against reference summaries; demonstrates the same shapes as CAIL/LBox generalize across CJK jurisdictions with only table/language swaps.
rows.proof: Korean case corpora.

rows.name: Legal RAG Bench (Isaacus)
rows.families: passage retrieval; grounded long-form legal QA; error attribution
rows.requires: A firm knowledge-base tool over a chunked practice manual with per-question gold passage IDs. The error-decomposition protocol (retrieval ceiling analysis) is the transferable asset: a simulation world can adopt the same hierarchical error taxonomy to attribute agent task failures to tool-use vs reasoning.
rows.proof: Grounded determination over a seeded corpus with enforced reads is hosted (discovery-retrieval tasks task_186–task_193 (8 tasks)). Passage-level retrieval at real-corpus scale (thousands of documents) is not — the world's corpus is 205 documents by design.

rows.name: LegalCiteBench
rows.families: citation retrieval; citation completion; citation error detection; case matching; case verification/correction
rows.requires: A citator tool backed by a case table (name, reporter cite, holding, treatment) — the world's 'Westlaw'. Task shape: cite-check a draft brief; grading is exact-match on citation strings and support labels. Directly hostable as a verifiable QA gate on any drafting task the firm world already runs.
rows.proof: Closed by the citation-audit pack (task_257–task_257 (1 tasks)): a verified citation registry, a brief table of authorities containing one absent citation and one superseded-for-the-proposition citation, and a policy forbidding memory verification; graded on the unsafe-citation count.

rows.name: LegalEval (SemEval-2023 Task 6)
rows.families: rhetorical role labeling; legal NER; judgment prediction with explanation
rows.requires: Judgment documents with sentence-level gold labels; hostable as litigation-analysis subtasks (structure an opinion before summarizing it) with deterministic per-sentence grading.
rows.proof: Judgment-prediction-with-explanation shape hosted via rule-application reviews (legalbench tasks task_201–task_214 (14 tasks): pinned outcome + rationale grounded in required reads). Span-level rhetorical-role labeling and NER are not record-level outcomes; hostable only via a per-span evidence-record pack.

rows.name: LegalEval-Q
rows.families: legal text quality scoring
rows.requires: Useful for calibrating the firm world's LLM judge: gold quality ratings let you validate that the judge's style/quality criteria correlate with human legal-writing judgments.
rows.proof: Scores prose quality of legal text — requires an LLM/human judge; deterministic verifiers grade records, not style.

rows.name: LegalHalBench
rows.families: hallucination-audited legal QA
rows.requires: A statute ground-truth table to verify every statute the agent cites exists and says what's claimed — an automatic hallucination detector the firm world can run over any deliverable that cites law.
rows.proof: Chinese corpus (the abstention shape itself is hosted in English: task_194–task_200 (7 tasks)).

rows.name: LegalLens (2024 shared task)
rows.families: violation NER; violation-resolution NLI
rows.requires: Hostable as class-action intake triage: an inbox of consumer complaints, an entity-extraction deliverable with F1 grading against gold spans, and a matching table linking complaints to open matters. Deterministic span/label grading.
rows.proof: Closed by the violation-screening pack (task_270–task_270 (1 tasks)): an employment intake summary screened against a five-slug claim matrix; both supported claims must be filed and the two unsupported categories are forbidden values.

rows.name: LexGenius
rows.families: legal knowledge MCQ; case reasoning; professional ethics; procedural judgment
rows.requires: Static MCQ — hostable only as a knowledge-check layer (e.g., associate 'training quizzes' inside the world); its Dimension-Task-Ability matrix is a useful capability taxonomy for tagging the world's tasks.
rows.proof: Chinese corpora.

rows.name: LexRAG
rows.families: conversational statute retrieval; multi-turn consultation response generation
rows.requires: A client-intake dialogue engine (simulated client turns) plus a statutes retrieval tool; grading combines retrieval gold per turn with response metrics. Gives the firm world its 'client consultation' task shape with per-turn verifiable retrieval anchors.
rows.proof: Chinese multi-turn consultation.

rows.name: LexRubric
rows.families: open-ended legal generation with diagnostic rubrics
rows.requires: Another rubric-taxonomy donor: per-dimension diagnostic rubrics (vs Harvey's all-pass binary) let the firm world report which capability dimension failed, improving flaky-task boundary evidence.
rows.proof: Rubric-scored open-ended generation — needs an LLM judge by construction.

rows.name: LLeQA
rows.families: long-form grounded legal QA; statute retrieval
rows.requires: Statutes table + retrieval tool + long-form answer grading (article-grounding is the verifiable part). Template for the firm world's 'research memo with pinpoint statutory citations' tasks where cited-article IDs are deterministically checkable.
rows.proof: French statutory corpus.

rows.name: Magis-Bench
rows.families: judicial-level drafting and review; judicial sentence drafting; discursive legal analysis (multi-turn)
rows.requires: Low direct fit (Brazilian judiciary), but its multi-judge-panel grading with reported inter-judge agreement is a robustness upgrade over Harvey LAB's single-judge scheme; a world adopting LLM-judged drafting tasks should replicate the panel + agreement-stat protocol.
rows.proof: Portuguese judicial corpora + judged discursive drafting.

rows.name: MASLegalBench
rows.families: IRAC-decomposed deductive reasoning; multi-agent role decomposition; GDPR compliance analysis
rows.requires: Deterministic MCQ grading; hostable as a data-privacy practice-group task line: world needs GDPR text + case-file documents and supports assigning subtasks to specialist sub-agents; the IRAC step structure gives natural intermediate checkpoints for process grading.
rows.proof: IRAC deductive rule application is hosted (legalbench pack task_201–task_214 (14 tasks): rule memo + fact pattern → pinned conclusion, edge cases included). Multi-agent role decomposition is not (single-agent world).

rows.name: NitiBench
rows.families: RAG legal QA; tax-case reasoning
rows.requires: Statute corpus + gold-cited answers; its RAG-vs-long-context ablation protocol is reusable for deciding which firm-world tasks need retrieval tools vs stuffed context.
rows.proof: Thai legal corpus.

rows.name: ObliQA / RegNLP RIRAG
rows.families: regulatory passage retrieval; obligation-grounded answer generation
rows.requires: A regulations corpus tool plus compliance-question task shape: 'what must our client do under these rules?' Gold passage IDs give the verifiable core; RePASs-style obligation-coverage scoring is adoptable for the world's compliance-memo tasks.
rows.proof: Closed by the obliqa-regulatory-obligations pack (task_253–task_255 (3 tasks)): rulebook chapters (SAR deadlines, client-money reconciliation intervals, client classification) plus a client query file; determinations pinned, with an absent-provision abstention task.

rows.name: PLawBench
rows.families: legal consultation; case analysis; document generation
rows.requires: Harvey-LAB-style rubric grading applied to consultation and case analysis; the firm world can import its rubric taxonomy (issue identification, fact spotting, document coherence) as additional criterion types for its LLM-judge, and its 13 scenario frames as matter templates.
rows.proof: Chinese corpora.

rows.name: SARA (StAtutory Reasoning Assessment)
rows.families: statutory entailment; numeric tax liability computation
rows.requires: A statutes/rules document set plus client fact-pattern intake records; task shape 'compute the client's liability under these sections and show which subsections applied'. Verifier is exact-dollar comparison (±10% variant used in LegalBench) or Prolog execution — no judge needed. Note: sara_entailment/sara_numeric slices already appear inside LegalBench (inventory item), but the standalone corpus with Prolog gold is richer.
rows.proof: Statutory rule-to-number computation is hosted by the damages-computation pack (task_167–task_173 (7 tasks): multi-step arithmetic from stated rules/facts, exact amounts pinned) and statutory entailment by legalbench rule-application (task_201–task_214 (14 tasks), pinned outcomes).

rows.name: STARD
rows.families: statute retrieval from layperson queries
rows.requires: Same substrate as BSARD; its distinctive asset is client-voice query phrasing — useful for making the firm world's simulated-client messages realistically non-legal while keeping retrieval gold verifiable.
rows.proof: Chinese statute retrieval.

rows.name: Summarization cluster (Multi-LexSum, CaseSumm, EurLexSum, UK/IN-Abs)
rows.families: multi-document case summarization; granularity-controlled summarization
rows.requires: Matter folders with many source documents plus gold summaries at multiple lengths — maps to the firm world's 'brief the partner in one paragraph / full memo' dual deliverables; grading via reference-based metrics plus judge.
rows.proof: Summary quality is judged-prose territory; deterministic verifiers cannot grade faithfulness/coverage of free-text summaries without gold-key reduction that changes the task.

rows.name: TAR stopping-rule research line (QBCB, Kneedle, GRLStop, point-process stopping)
rows.families: review-stopping certification; recall estimation under sampling budget
rows.requires: A crisp deterministic task for the world: agent runs a review campaign, must file a 'certification memo' with a stopping point and stated recall; grader knows true relevance labels and checks whether the certified recall claim held. Needs only the corpus + oracle infrastructure already listed for TREC tasks.
rows.proof: Stopping-rule certification requires statistical estimation over corpora of thousands+; a 205-document world cannot pose the substance.

rows.name: TREC Legal Track (2006-2011)
rows.families: responsive-document-retrieval; high-recall search; relevance assessment appeal/adjudication; privilege-aware production
rows.requires: A large email+attachment corpus table (custodian, date, thread, SHA1 hash, file type), a mock complaint + document-request text per matter, a search/query tool over the corpus, a coding tool (responsive/non-responsive/privileged per doc), and a grader computing recall/precision/F1 against sealed gold relevance judgments with sampling-based estimation. Deterministic grading if gold labels exist.
rows.proof: Responsive-review at 7M-document scale (Enron); corpus-scale mechanic absent.

rows.name: TREC Total Recall Track (2015-2016)
rows.families: continuous active learning (CAL); review-budget management; stopping decision
rows.requires: A relevance-oracle tool (returns gold label per submitted doc id, with a call counter as the cost meter), corpus table, and deterministic recall@effort grading. Maps perfectly to a law-firm world: 'associate review budget' = oracle calls; agent decides which docs to route to review and when to stop. Fully deterministic and repeatable.
rows.proof: Continuous active learning over large corpora; same scale mechanic.

rows.name: TriBench-Ko
rows.families: summarization; precedent retrieval; issue extraction; evidence analysis; risk auditing
rows.requires: Its risk-audit matrix is the transferable design: the firm world can attach risk-channel probes (rerun with perturbed prompts, measure non-determinism/omission) to existing tasks — directly relevant to boundary-proving flaky tasks.
rows.proof: Korean corpora.

rows.name: CAIL (China AI & Law Challenge, 2018–2025 umbrella)
rows.families: judgment prediction; similar case matching; judicial reading comprehension; argument mining; summarization; law-article prediction; charge identification; sentence/prison-term estimation; legal judgment prediction (law article / charge / prison term); similar case matching & 类案检索 case retrieval (lajs); legal element extraction (要素识别); judicial reading comprehension (ydlj/CJRC); judicial examination QA (sfks, JEC-QA-derived); judicial summarization (sfzy); information extraction (xxcq); argument understanding / 论辩理解 (lblj); event detection (sjjc/LEVEN, 2022); LLM/agent-era tracks (2023–2025, e.g. legal consultation)
rows.requires: A Chinese-law wing of the firm world: a criminal/civil docket table where each matter row carries a fact-description document plus hidden gold fields (statute IDs, charge labels, sentence months, element tags, event spans); a statute table (刑法/民法典 articles with IDs) exposed via a lookup tool; a precedent database with a similarity-search tool for SCM/lajs-shaped tasks; task shapes = intake-assessment memos whose required fields (predicted charge, cited article IDs, sentence range, matched precedent IDs) are graded deterministically against the gold columns.
rows.proof: Chinese court corpora across all tracks (the judgment-prediction SHAPE is hosted in English via legalbench rule-application).

rows.name: COLIEE (Competition on Legal Information Extraction/Entailment)
rows.families: case-law retrieval; case entailment; statute retrieval; statute entailment QA; judgment prediction (pilot); case entailment (paragraph-level); statutory entailment QA; tort/rationale prediction; Task 1: case law retrieval (find noticed/supporting cases for a query case); Task 2: case entailment (identify the paragraph(s) of a precedent that entail a new-case fragment); Task 3: statute retrieval (find Civil Code articles relevant to a bar-exam statement); Task 4: statute entailment (Y/N: does the retrieved article entail the statement); 2025 pilot: legal judgment prediction for Japanese tort cases
rows.requires: Two firm-world libraries: (1) a precedent corpus table (thousands of case texts) with a search tool, gold noticed-case lists per query matter — task shape 'compile the table of authorities for this brief', F1-graded; (2) a statute table (Civil Code articles with IDs) with lookup tool, gold relevant-article sets and Y/N entailment labels — task shape 'confirm whether client's position is supported by statute, citing articles'; both need deterministic set-comparison graders and per-task gold-ID columns.
rows.proof: Statute/case ENTAILMENT shape is hosted (legalbench tasks task_201–task_214 (14 tasks): rule + facts → pinned conclusion). Case-law retrieval over a real decisions corpus is not (small seeded corpus only).

rows.name: Philip C. Jessup International Law Moot Court Competition (+ GenAI Jessup study)
rows.families: written memorial drafting for Applicant and Respondent from a fixed case record; oral pleading rounds (human); rubric-scored evaluation (published 1–100-per-criterion scoring rubric)
rows.requires: A ready-made 'both-sides drafting' task shape: one matter record, two opposing deliverables (Applicant/Respondent memorials), graded against the published ILSA rubric dimensions via LLM judge plus a deterministic citation-verification pass (every cited authority must exist in the world's authorities table) — the citation-hallucination failure mode the study found is exactly what a closed-world authorities table can verify deterministically.
rows.proof: Human-judged memorial prose + oral rounds.

rows.name: Willem C. Vis International Commercial Arbitration Moot
rows.families: memorandum for Claimant and Respondent (CISG + arbitral procedure issues); oral arbitration hearings (human)
rows.requires: Transactional-disputes variant of the moot shape: problem record decomposed into world documents (contract, correspondence exhibits, procedural orders), a CISG/arbitration-rules statute table for citation verification, two-sided memoranda deliverables scored on issue coverage rubrics; procedural orders arriving mid-task naturally instantiate the world's 'new information drops during the matter' mechanic.
rows.proof: Human-judged memoranda + oral hearings.

rows.name: AnnoCaseLaw
rows.families: annotated judgment prediction
rows.requires: Element-level gold annotations enable deterministic grading of issue-element analysis in litigation tasks (did the memo address each negligence element the gold marks present?).
rows.proof: Closed by the appeal-outcome pack (task_256–task_256 (1 tasks)): trial-court record summary plus an appellate-standard memo whose disposition rule must be applied to a preserved-but-unaddressed carve-out; outcome pinned reverse, affirm forbidden.

rows.name: CAIL2018 (Legal Judgment Prediction dataset)
rows.families: law article prediction; charge identification; prison-term estimation
rows.requires: Criminal-matter intake queue: matters table with fact_description docs and gold columns (article_ids[], charge_labels[], sentence_months); statute lookup tool over a Criminal Law articles table; task shape = charging/sentencing exposure memo with three machine-checkable fields; supports massive task sampling since 2.68M gold-labeled cases exist.
rows.proof: Chinese judgments corpus.

rows.name: CAIL2019-SCM (Similar Case Matching)
rows.families: triplet similar-case matching
rows.requires: Precedent-research task shape: a precedents table holding full case texts; a 'compare precedents' assignment where the associate must recommend which of two candidate precedents better supports the client matter; gold binary answer per triplet enables deterministic pass/fail; needs only document storage + read tools.
rows.proof: Chinese similar-case corpus.

rows.name: CJRC (Chinese Judicial Reading Comprehension, CAIL2019 track)
rows.families: extractive span QA over judgments; yes/no QA; unanswerable detection
rows.requires: Document-QA task shape inside the firm: judgment PDFs/texts filed under matters; client-question tickets whose gold answers are spans in the filed document (plus deliberately unanswerable tickets to test abstention); grading via span-overlap F1 — the world needs a per-question gold-span table and a read/grep toolset over matter files.
rows.proof: Chinese judicial reading comprehension.

rows.name: Court View Generation corpora (Ye et al. 2018; C3VG-style, CAIL-derived)
rows.families: court view / judicial rationale generation (本院认为 section)
rows.requires: Drafting task shape with reference-based grading: matters carry facts plus a withheld gold rationale text; task = draft the reasoning section of a judgment or an internal 'anticipated court view' memo; world needs a text-similarity grader (ROUGE/BERTScore) plus keyword/charge-consistency checks — the one CAIL-family shape that is generation-graded rather than label-graded.
rows.proof: Chinese court-view generation (also judged-prose).

rows.name: EDRM Enron Email Data Set v2
rows.families: ingestion/extraction; deduplication (hash-based); load-file generation; custodian/date culling; PII/privilege screening
rows.requires: File-store of raw PST/EML/attachment files with per-file gold metadata (SHA1, custodian, dates, family relationships), tools for extraction and hashing, and deterministic verification: output load file diffed field-by-field against gold EDRM XML; dedupe counts and family integrity checked exactly.
rows.proof: The review half is hosted: responsiveness/privilege-style classification over a seeded email corpus with distractors (discovery-retrieval tasks task_186–task_193 (8 tasks)), production-cost allocation (the ESI cost-allocation tasks in task_167–task_173 (7 tasks)). The processing half (hash dedup, load-file generation, culling at corpus scale) is e-discovery software mechanics the world does not model.

rows.name: GerLayQA (German layperson legal QA)
rows.families: layperson legal QA with paragraph grounding; layperson question answering grounded in statute paragraphs; statute paragraph retrieval
rows.requires: Client-intake hotline shape for a German desk: intake tickets with a lay question, gold code-paragraph IDs, and a reference lawyer answer; a statute table of code paragraphs with lookup tool; two-part grading — cited-paragraph set match (deterministic) + answer rubric (LLM judge); 21k items give broad sampling coverage.
rows.proof: German statute-grounded QA.

rows.name: ILDC for CJPE (Indian Legal Documents Corpus)
rows.families: binary appeal-outcome prediction; decision explanation (gold rationale spans)
rows.requires: Appellate-risk-assessment shape: matters table of Indian SC case files with the outcome removed and stored as a gold binary column plus gold rationale spans; task = 'advise the client on appeal prospects, citing the passages that drive your view'; grading = binary outcome match (deterministic) + rationale-span overlap (ROUGE/occlusion-style) — gives the world an explanation-graded family.
rows.proof: Same pack as annocaselaw (task_256–task_256 (1 tasks)): English appeal-outcome prediction with the rationale grounded in required reads. The Indian-language corpus itself remains out of scope.

rows.name: LawFlow (minnesotanlp)
rows.families: end-to-end workflow simulation; process-trace comparison; entity-formation matter handling (intake → structure choice → drafting); workflow planning/replanning
rows.requires: Anchors process-level grading: a world hosting formation matters (client facts table, state filing requirements, operating-agreement templates) can score agents on action-sequence similarity to LawFlow human traces in addition to output correctness — the only public gold-process dataset found for transactional work.
rows.proof: Closed by the lawflow-entity-formation pack (task_250–task_252 (3 tasks)): LawFlow's real 48-step formation plan compressed to intake notes + decision-rule memo + filing checklist; entity choice against a contrary client preference, derived fee total, and the 83(b) date.

rows.name: LawInstruct
rows.families: instruction tuning corpus
rows.requires: Not hostable as tasks; relevant as training data for a firm-world-native baseline model (lawfirm-qwen fine-tuning) and as a catalog of 58 source datasets to mine for more task shapes.
rows.proof: Training corpus, not an evaluation — out of scope for a verifiable world.

rows.name: LegalQuAD (German legal extractive QA)
rows.families: extractive QA over German legal documents; QA-style retrieval
rows.requires: Small German document-QA ticket shape: client questions each mapped to a filed German statute/decision document and a gold answer span; needs per-ticket gold spans and a span-F1 verifier; too small to carry a task family alone — best used to seed a German-language variant of the CJRC-style ticket shape.
rows.proof: German extractive QA corpus.

rows.name: LeNER-Br (Brazilian legal NER)
rows.families: legal NER (incl. Legislation and Jurisprudence entity classes)
rows.requires: Citation-index building shape: task = extract every statute and precedent reference from a filed Brazilian document into a structured citations table; gold token/span annotations per document power a deterministic span-F1 verifier; small size means it seeds a shape rather than a large task pool.
rows.proof: Portuguese NER corpus.

rows.name: LEVEN (CAIL2022 legal event detection)
rows.families: legal event detection (trigger identification + typing)
rows.requires: Chronology/issue-coding task shape: matter documents with a hidden gold event-annotation table (doc_id, span, event_type); task = produce a structured case chronology or event log; verifier joins the agent's extracted events against gold spans/types — needs an events schema and span-level deterministic matcher in the world's grading harness.
rows.proof: Chinese event-detection corpus.

rows.name: MultiEURLEX (multilingual EU-law classification; LEXTREME sub-dataset)
rows.families: multi-label EUROVOC topic classification; cross-lingual zero-shot transfer
rows.requires: Regulatory-watch shape: an EU-legislation feed table where each incoming instrument must be tagged with practice-area/topic labels routed to the right firm team; gold EUROVOC label sets give a deterministic multi-label F1 verifier; already indirectly covered via LEXTREME in the inventory but worth a standalone entry because the routing shape is distinct.
rows.proof: 23-language EU-law classification corpus.

rows.name: Pile of Law / MultiLegalPile / LexFiles (corpora)
rows.families: legal corpus
rows.requires: Raw material: realistic document filler for the firm world's DMS (making retrieval non-trivial), and source text for authoring new synthetic matters with authentic register.
rows.proof: Pretraining corpora, not evaluations.

rows.name: Swiss-Judgment-Prediction
rows.families: binary judgment outcome prediction (approval/dismissal); robustness/fairness slicing by language, canton, year, legal area
rows.requires: Multilingual appeal-triage shape: docket rows in three languages with gold outcome column plus metadata columns enabling per-slice scoreboards (language/canton/area) — the metadata makes it uniquely suited to a world that wants fairness/robustness dashboards; only needs document store, gold labels, and slice-aware aggregation in the grader.
rows.proof: German/French/Italian court corpora.

rows.name: VICTOR (Brazilian Supreme Court document dataset)
rows.families: document type classification; multi-label process theme assignment
rows.requires: Mailroom/docketing task shape: an inbound-documents queue where each uploaded file must be typed and routed (doc_type field, theme labels) before matter work proceeds; world needs a document-metadata table with hidden gold type/theme columns and a deterministic label-match verifier — a natural 'paralegal ops' family that stress-tests high-volume triage rather than reasoning.
rows.proof: Portuguese supreme-court documents.

rows.name: A2J Author
rows.families: guided interview design; court form population; SRL-facing plain-language question drafting
rows.requires: Same hosting shape as docassemble but interviews are XML-based; a world can anchor 'convert this court form + statute into a working interview' tasks; grading via fixed personas run through the interview and exact-match on assembled form fields. Value is mainly as task-shape/corpus source, not runnable OSS (free but not fully open-source).
rows.proof: Guided-interview + court-form-template runtime absent.

rows.name: Appellate practice management
rows.families: notice-of-appeal deadline computation with tolling motions; record designation and transcript ordering; briefing schedule computation and recalculation on extensions; brief compliance checking (word count, certificates, appendix); oral argument and mandate tracking
rows.requires: Tables: appeals (case, court below, judgment_date, NOA filed_date, appellate case_no, status), tolling_motions (type, filed, decided — changes NOA deadline), briefing_deadlines, transcript_orders, record_designations, compliance_checklists (word_count, certificates booleans). Rule data: FRAP time table + one or two circuit variants. Task shapes: judgment entered date X with a Rule 59 motion decided date Y → compute correct NOA deadline (tolling logic is a classic boundary case) and the full briefing chain; check a brief metadata record against limits; deterministic date/limit verification.
rows.proof: Notice-of-appeal computation with entry-vs-minute-order discrimination and holiday rollover (task_174–task_179 (6 tasks)) plus the appellate disposition assessment (task_256–task_256 (1 tasks)). Tolling-motion recomputation and record designation remain unhosted.

rows.name: Calendaring / docketing with court-rule deadlines
rows.families: trigger-event identification from documents; rules-based deadline computation (FRCP 6 / state analogues); deadline-chain generation; cascade recomputation on trigger change; reminder and assignment management; missed-deadline detection/audit
rows.requires: Tables: docket_events (matter, trigger_type, trigger_date), deadlines (event, rule cite, computed_date, assigned_to, status), court_rules (rule set per jurisdiction: offset days, day type, service-method adders), holidays calendar. Tools: deadline calculator, calendar CRUD, rule lookup. Task shapes: serve a complaint on date X in jurisdiction Y → agent must produce the exact gold set of dated deadlines (answer due, initial disclosures, expert disclosure 90 days pre-trial, dispositive motion cutoff); then move the trial date and verify every dependent deadline was recomputed. Fully deterministic verification — the strongest fit in the whole list for programmatic grading.
rows.proof: Closed by the deadline-computation pack (task_174–task_179 (6 tasks)): SRCP-6-style computation from trigger documents — personal vs mail service, filing vs service triggers, weekend/holiday rollover, mail-day ordering, briefing-chain day counts — with naive-method dates as forbidden traps and a no-trigger abstention task.

rows.name: Client intake + conflicts checking
rows.families: conflict search across parties/matters/contacts; adverse-party and related-entity identification; conflict waiver drafting; declination letter drafting; intake-form data entry and validation; lead-to-matter pipeline reporting
rows.requires: Tables: contacts (persons + entities with aliases, former names, corporate family links), matters (with party roles: client, adverse, co-party, witness), leads/intake_forms, conflict_checks (search terms, hits, resolution, timestamp, resolver), waivers. Tools: name search with fuzzy matching over all tables; conflict-check record creation; matter-open action that must be gated on a completed clean/resolved check. Task shapes: seed a latent conflict (subsidiary of an existing adverse party, former client under a maiden name) and verify the agent finds it, records the hit, and blocks or waives before opening; deterministic verification = conflict_checks row exists, hit list matches gold, matter status correct.
rows.proof: Conflicts workflow hosted end-to-end: conflict_cases chains with evidence/review/remediation creates (harvey_lab workflow tasks e.g. task_076, task_086, task_096 use legal_conflicts tools), conflicts-archive-gap abstention trap (the conflicts-archive-gap trap in task_194–task_200 (7 tasks)), adverse-party search via records-research tasks; matter opening chains (task_001 family).

rows.name: CLOC Core 12 (legal operations competency framework)
rows.families: outside-counsel spend analysis / e-billing audit; vendor RFP and panel management; matter intake and resourcing; knowledge-management curation; legal-tech rollout planning
rows.requires: Tables for invoices (UTBMS/LEDES billing codes!), timekeepers, rates, matters, vendors, budgets. Deterministic task family: audit LEDES invoice lines against outside-counsel billing guidelines (block billing, rate caps, staffing limits) — exact rule-violation lists are machine-gradable. CLOC maturity language supplies realistic scenario framing.
rows.proof: Spend/e-billing review hosted (legal_billing chains: invoice_reviews + amount histories, e.g. task_015; fee true-up computation the fee true-up task in task_167–task_173 (7 tasks)). Vendor RFP management, KM, and resourcing competencies are not modeled.

rows.name: Closing binders / transaction closing management
rows.families: closing checklist creation and status tracking; signature packet assembly and tracking; conditions-precedent verification gate; executed-document compilation (signature pages merged, exhibits attached); closing binder indexing and assembly; post-closing deliverables tracking
rows.requires: Tables: deals (parties, target close date, status), checklist_items (document, workstream, responsible, status, CP flag), signatories, signature_pages (doc × signer, status collected/released), binder_index. Documents: a corpus of deal documents in versions (unsigned drafts, signature pages, exhibits) so compilation is a real file operation. Task shapes: pre-closing audit — identify the 2 seeded unmet CPs and the missing signature page and block closing; assemble the binder whose index and file set must exactly match gold (every executed doc complete with its exhibits); verification = checklist state machine + file-manifest diff.
rows.proof: Closed by the closing-binder pack (task_258–task_258 (1 tasks)): conditions-precedent checklist with one outstanding third-party consent, plus a signature report whose outstanding item is a deliverable rather than a condition — the distinction is what the determination grades.

rows.name: Contract Lifecycle Management stage model + OpenCLM
rows.families: contract intake triage; template+clause-library drafting; approval-matrix routing; post-execution obligation extraction; renewal-date monitoring
rows.requires: Tables: contract records with lifecycle status enum, clause library, approval matrix (role x contract-type x value thresholds), obligations (party, action, due date), counterparties. Tools: draft/redline editors, route-for-approval, e-sign stub. Grading: status-transition legality is machine-checkable (did the agent skip a required approver?), obligation rows exact-match vs gold. Complements Harvey LAB's contracting family with process-state verification instead of LLM-judged prose.
rows.proof: Draft/negotiate/redline stages hosted (deep-drafting tasks task_180–task_185 (6 tasks); cuad task_157–task_166 (10 tasks); spa task_225–task_231 (7 tasks)). Intake triage, approval-matrix routing, and post-execution obligation tracking are not seeded; an obligations pack would close the biggest missing stage.

rows.name: Court e-filing (CM/ECF)
rows.families: docket-event selection and PDF assembly; PII redaction compliance check; filing submission and NEF processing; service-list management (registered vs paper-service parties); deficiency-notice correction and re-filing; incoming NEF triage into docket + deadlines
rows.requires: Tables: court_dockets (case_no, entries with number/date/type/filer/text), filings (status draft/submitted/accepted/rejected + rejection reason), service_lists, NEF notifications queue, fee ledger. Simulated ECF tool: submit(case, event_type, docs) → validates event-type match, PDF/redaction flags, returns NEF or deficiency; incoming-NEF feed the agent must triage. Task shapes: file an opposition brief before the midnight deadline choosing the right event code; process an inbound NEF (order granting motion) into internal docket entries plus the recomputed deadline chain; verification = docket rows and deadline rows vs gold, rejection loop handled.
rows.proof: Closed by the court-efiling pack (task_259–task_259 (1 tasks)): local-rules excerpt (LR 5.2 redaction, LR 7.1 page limits, LR 5.4 filing window) against a draft brief that is within the page limit but exposes a full account number and birth date — the determination must be redact_before_filing, not file_as_is or seek_leave.

rows.name: Deposition management
rows.families: notice vs subpoena selection and drafting; scheduling against availability and discovery cutoff; vendor booking (reporter/videographer); transcript intake and errata tracking; deposition exhibit numbering and tracking; transcript summarization/designations
rows.requires: Tables: depositions (matter, deponent, party/non-party flag, date, location, status), notices/subpoenas (served_date, method), vendors/bookings, transcripts (received_date, errata_due, errata entries page/line/change), depo_exhibits (number, description, source doc), witness availability calendar. Documents: notice/subpoena templates, a transcript text for summarization tasks. Task shapes: set up a third-party deposition (must choose subpoena, not notice, and calendar it before the discovery cutoff), then process an errata sheet into the transcript record; verification = correct instrument type, dates inside cutoff, errata rows match gold.
rows.proof: Closed by the deposition-management pack (task_260–task_261 (2 tasks)): party-vs-non-party compulsion (notice has no effect on a non-party; Rule 45 subpoena required) and latest-compliant-date scheduling against the fact-discovery cutoff, with the client-preferred but non-compliant date as a forbidden value.

rows.name: Discovery management (requests, responses, privilege logs, meet-and-confer)
rows.families: discovery request/response tracking with deadlines; response drafting with per-request objections; responsiveness + privilege document review; privilege log construction; production logging with Bates ranges; meet-and-confer letter drafting and dispute tracking; motion-to-compel deadline management
rows.requires: Tables: discovery_sets (type, served_date, service_method, response_due, status), requests (set_id, number, text, response, objections), documents corpus (custodian, date, author, recipients, privilege flags — gold labels hidden), privilege_log (doc, date, author, recipients, basis, description), productions (Bates start/end, date, volume), disputes/meet_confer_log. Documents: seeded corpus of ~50-200 matter documents including attorney-client emails, work product drafts, and non-privileged lookalikes. Task shapes: respond to a 25-request RFP set — verifier checks every withheld gold-privileged doc appears on the log with adequate fields, no privileged doc in the production Bates range, response served before computed deadline. Mix of deterministic (deadlines, Bates, log completeness) and rubric (objection quality) grading.
rows.proof: Hosted: discovery request chains (litigation_discovery tasks e.g. task_015 family), responsiveness/privilege-style classification with enforced reads (task_186–task_193 (8 tasks)), production-cost allocation (task_169–170). Not hosted: per-request objection drafting graded at answer level, privilege-log generation.

rows.name: docassemble
rows.families: interview authoring (YAML logic); document assembly (template → PDF/DOCX); client intake automation; conditional legal-logic encoding
rows.requires: A docassemble server (or emulated interview runtime) as a world service; client-fact tables to feed interviews; gold output documents. Grading is deterministic: run the interview with fixed answer sets and diff assembled document fields against gold. ALKiln (below) supplies the exact test format.
rows.proof: Interview/document-assembly runtime absent.

rows.name: Document management with versioning and ethical walls
rows.families: document profiling and filing; version check-out/check-in discipline; email-to-matter filing; ethical-wall setup after lateral hire or conflict waiver; audit-trail investigation (who accessed what); retention/destruction runs
rows.requires: Tables: documents (workspace/matter, doc_id, version_no, checked_out_by, profile metadata), workspaces, access_control (walls: user/group × matter deny rules), audit_log (user, doc, action, timestamp), retention_policies. Tools: file/checkout/checkin, search constrained by ACL, wall creation, audit query. Task shapes: erect an ethical wall around matter X for screened attorney Y then prove via audit log no access; reconstruct which version of an agreement was sent to the counterparty on a date from version history; verification = ACL rows, version chain integrity, audit-log query results match gold.
rows.proof: Superseded-version discipline is a core graded behavior (deep-drafting superseding-instruction task; superseded-draft forbidden-value traps across maud/spa/damages packs; update_matter_documents_title tool). Ethical walls and check-out/check-in are not modeled.

rows.name: Engagement letters and fee agreements
rows.families: engagement letter drafting from template + matter facts; fee-arrangement selection and rate-table population; e-signature status tracking; non-engagement/declination letters; retainer collection into trust
rows.requires: Tables: engagement_letters (matter_id, fee_type, rates, scope text, status draft/sent/signed, signed_date), templates library, rate cards per timekeeper/client, trust_transactions (initial retainer deposit). Documents: template .docx with merge fields; gold letters for comparison. Tools: document generation/merge, signature-status update, trust deposit posting. Task shapes: draft letter whose fee terms must match the matter record exactly; verify merge-field values, correct fee clause chosen, retainer deposit row posted to the right client trust ledger; billing later blocked if letter unsigned.
rows.proof: Closed by the engagement-letters pack (task_262–task_263 (2 tasks)): a client-requested contingency on a pure defense engagement (impermissible — no recovery) where the policy directs the nearest permissible alternative, plus the countersigned-letter fee threshold.

rows.name: Expert witness management (FRCP 26(a)(2))
rows.families: expert retention and engagement tracking; disclosure deadline calendaring (90/30-day rules); report completeness check against the six 26(a)(2)(B) elements; prior-testimony and conflict screening; supplementation tracking; Daubert motion deadline management; expert invoice processing against budget
rows.requires: Tables: experts (name, field, rates, retained_matter, side), expert_engagements (agreement date, budget, invoices), disclosures (type initial/rebuttal, due_date, served_date), report_checklists (six boolean element fields), prior_testimony records, deadlines linkage to scheduling-order table. Documents: a draft expert report with a seeded missing element (e.g., no compensation statement). Task shapes: given a scheduling order and trial date, compute and calendar all expert deadlines and flag the report deficiency; verification = deadline rows exact, checklist booleans match gold defect.
rows.proof: Closed by the expert-witness-management pack (task_264–task_265 (2 tasks)): Rule 26(a)(2)(B) six-element completeness check against a package missing the 10-year publications list, plus the 90-days-before-trial disclosure date computed from a scheduling order.

rows.name: Juriscraper + RECAP/CourtListener (Free Law Project docket stack)
rows.families: docket sheet parsing to structured entries; new-filing alert triage; document fetch + matter-file routing; opinion metadata extraction
rows.requires: World needs courts/cases/docket_entries/documents tables with timestamped incoming filings (simulated PACER), an alert-subscription tool, and tasks like 'monitor matter M, docket every new entry, calendar any triggered deadlines'; grading deterministic via exact docket-entry and calendar-row comparison.
rows.proof: Docket-entry triage and routing hosted (litigation_dockets chains, docket_entries table). Live scraping of real court systems is out of scope by design.

rows.name: KYC/AML client screening
rows.families: identity verification and document collection; beneficial-ownership chain resolution; sanctions/PEP/adverse-media list screening with false-positive adjudication; risk rating and EDD escalation; ongoing monitoring alerts; suspicious-activity escalation and engagement blocking
rows.requires: Tables: clients, ownership_edges (entity→owner %, layered so UBO requires graph traversal), screening_lists (sanctions/PEP entries with near-miss name variants), screenings (subject, list hits, adjudication true/false positive, rationale), risk_ratings, cdd_files (documents collected, status), monitoring_alerts. Tools: list-match search (fuzzy), ownership traversal, risk-score computation. Task shapes: onboard a company whose 3-layer ownership hides a 30% sanctioned UBO behind a nominee — agent must traverse to the UBO, adjudicate the near-miss name correctly, rate high-risk, and block engagement; verification = UBO set, hit adjudications, and engagement status vs gold.
rows.proof: Closed by the kyc-aml-screening pack (task_266–task_267 (2 tasks)): onboarding file with an unidentified 45% corporate-nominee layer, screening results, and a policy memo whose three-way vocabulary (cleared | hold_beneficial_ownership | declined) is graded — both over-clearing and over-declining are forbidden values.

rows.name: Matter opening (new business intake)
rows.families: matter record creation with required-field validation; staffing and rate assignment; SOL date computation and calendaring; DMS workspace creation; matter numbering schemes
rows.requires: Tables: matters (number, client_id, practice_area, responsible_atty, billing_atty, status, open_date, SOL_date, jurisdiction, court, billing_arrangement, client_matter_ids for e-billing), users/timekeepers, rate_assignments, tasks, calendar. Gating logic: matter cannot open without clean conflict check + signed engagement letter (referential checks the verifier can assert). Task shapes: given an intake packet, open the matter with every required field correct; deterministic verification against gold matter row; failure modes = missing SOL date, wrong rate card, opening despite unresolved conflict.
rows.proof: Matter-opening chains are the world's largest family: legal_matters list→get→create workflows with required-field validation enforced by tool signatures (task_001, task_063, task_067, task_075, task_085, task_095 + banking/bankruptcy/arbitration variants).

rows.name: Outside-counsel-guidelines compliance billing (LEDES/UTBMS)
rows.families: UTBMS task/activity coding of narratives; OCG rule application and violation flagging; LEDES 1998B file generation and validation; rate-cap and staffing compliance; rejection triage and appeal drafting; accrual and budget reporting to client
rows.requires: Tables: time_entries with codes, client_billing_guidelines (machine-readable rule set: banned codes, rate caps per timekeeper class, max hours/day, pre-approval list), ledes_invoices (raw file text + parse status), rejections (line, rule violated), timekeeper classifications. Tools: LEDES validator (field count, delimiter, arithmetic: sum of line totals = invoice total), OCG rules engine simulating the client's e-billing platform. Task shapes: code and export a month of WIP for an OCG client — the simulated e-billing endpoint deterministically rejects any line violating the rule set; agent iterates until acceptance; verification = validator pass + zero gold-rule violations + arithmetic exact. Entirely deterministic and directly reusable as an executable-world verifier.
rows.proof: Billing review + fee-computation hosted (invoice_reviews chains; fee true-up the fee true-up task in task_167–task_173 (7 tasks); invoice status task_016-family). UTBMS narrative coding and LEDES file generation are not modeled.

rows.name: Settlement negotiation tracking
rows.families: demand/offer ledger maintenance; authority-limit compliance checking; Rule 68 offer-of-judgment deadline handling (14-day acceptance); settlement agreement drafting from negotiated terms; disbursement sheet computation (fees/liens/net); mediation logistics tracking
rows.requires: Tables: negotiations (matter, round, direction demand/offer, amount, terms, date, expiry, status), settlement_authority (client-approved floor/ceiling, date), liens (medical, subrogation amounts), settlements (final amount, terms), disbursements linking to trust ledger. Documents: settlement agreement/release templates. Task shapes: log a counteroffer and detect it exceeds authority → must seek client instruction rather than accept; compute a disbursement sheet where contingency fee %, costs, and liens must reconcile to the gross settlement to the penny and post correctly to trust; arithmetic and state-machine verification are fully deterministic.
rows.proof: Closed by the settlement-authority pack (task_268–task_269 (2 tasks)): client authority letter plus an offer ledger whose open offer sits $25,000 below the authority floor; graded on the accept-vs-escalate determination and the computed shortfall.

rows.name: Suffolk Document Assembly Line (court-form interview library)
rows.families: court-form completion end-to-end; e-filing packet preparation; interview localization/adaptation
rows.requires: Import real interview YAML as world content; simulated e-filing endpoint (accepts packet, validates required fields/signatures/fees); grade on packet-field exactness vs gold. Provides realistic pro-bono/clinic task lines for a law-firm world.
rows.proof: Court-form PDF completion runtime absent.

rows.name: TARexp (eugene-yang/tarexp)
rows.families: TAR workflow composition; stopping-rule selection/justification; cost-recall tradeoff analysis
rows.requires: Host as tasks where the agent operates a review campaign: tables for review batches, per-doc predicted scores, reviewer labels, per-hour review cost; agent must decide batch sizes and certify a defensible stopping point; grade deterministically on achieved recall vs cost against TARexp-computed optimal frontier.
rows.proof: TAR workflow composition requires corpus-scale active-learning mechanics.

rows.name: Time capture, prebill review, and invoicing
rows.families: time entry creation and coding; prebill generation from unbilled WIP; narrative-quality and duplicate review; write-down/write-off application; invoice finalization and AR posting; realization/WIP/aging reporting
rows.requires: Tables: time_entries (timekeeper, matter, date, hours, rate, narrative, task_code, activity_code, status unbilled/billed/written_off), expense_entries, prebills (line adjustments with reason codes), invoices (header + lines, totals, status), payments/AR, rate_cards with effective dates. Tools: prebill generation, line-item edit/write-down, invoice issue, aging report. Task shapes: generate the prebill for matter M for month N, catch the 3 seeded defects (duplicate entry, rate mismatch vs engagement letter, block-billed narrative), apply specified adjustments, issue invoice whose arithmetic and line set match gold; verification = exact table diff.
rows.proof: Invoice lifecycle hosted (update_invoices_status task_016-family; invoice_reviews chains; billing computations the fee true-up task in task_167–task_173 (7 tasks)). Time-entry capture and prebill generation from WIP are not seeded (no time-entries table).

rows.name: Trust / IOLTA accounting with three-way reconciliation
rows.families: trust deposit/disbursement posting; earned-fee transfer to operating; three-way reconciliation to the penny; discrepancy diagnosis (misposting, commingling, outstanding items); client ledger overdraft prevention; settlement disbursement sheets
rows.requires: Tables: trust_bank_transactions (bank-side statement lines), trust_ledger (book side: date, client, matter, payee, amount, check_no, cleared flag), client_trust_subledgers derived per client, operating_account, reconciliations (period, three balances, status, discrepancy notes). Tools: post transaction, mark cleared, run reconciliation report, transfer trust→operating. Task shapes: month-end close with seeded discrepancies (a $150 check posted to the wrong client, a deposit in transit, a disbursement exceeding one client's balance) — agent must produce a reconciliation where all three totals match and name each correcting entry. Penny-exact deterministic verification; the canonical flaky-boundary task since one wrong ledger row breaks the invariant sum(subledgers)=book=adjusted bank.
rows.proof: Closed on the v3 surface: trust ledgers are coherent by construction (funded before spent, kind/sign/memo correlated) with two deliberate overdrafts as the answer key; single-matter overdraft detection and the all-matters sweep are graded tasks (task_v3_015–task_v3_015 (1 tasks)).

rows.name: Awesome lists / meta-catalogs (maastrichtlawtech/awesome-legal-nlp, neelguha/legal-ml-datasets, openlegaldata/awesome-legal-data, Vaquill-AI/awesome-legaltech, Jeryi-Sun/LLM-and-Law)
rows.families: catalog
rows.requires: Monitoring feeds for new anchors; no world requirements. Additional entries enumerated there and not individually listed here: FSCS Swiss judgment prediction (85k), CJRC (50k Chinese QA), JUSTICE, Cambridge Law Corpus (258k UK cases), Super-SCOTUS, GLC, Contract Discovery, Contract Elements, FairLex, EU2UK/UK2EU, LEAD, LAR-ECHR, δ-Stance, PrivacyQA, IndicLegalQA, LEGAL-UQA, TOS;DR, BillSum, TL;DRLegal, BVA Cases.
rows.proof: Meta-catalogs, not evaluable capabilities.

rows.name: awesome-legal-skills (lawve-ai)
rows.families: playbook redline (draft→review→redline→negotiate); compliance gap analysis + roadmap; matter intake→plan→bill→close; litigation chronology from bundles; citation/source verification
rows.requires: Not a benchmark but the richest open catalog of agentic legal task procedures found; a world can mine its skill procedures as task specs (each skill's step list becomes the gold process) — hosting needs whatever each skill touches: matter tables, disclosure bundles, playbooks, billing records.
rows.proof: Its four playbooks map to live families: playbook redline (deep-drafting tasks task_180–task_185 (6 tasks)), compliance/risk review (cuad task_157–task_166 (10 tasks), maud task_215–task_224 (10 tasks)), matter intake→bill→close (legal_matters + billing chains), litigation checklists (litigation entity chains).

rows.name: ContraxSuite + LexNLP (LexPredict)
rows.families: structured field extraction from contracts; clause-type classification; portfolio-wide contract triage
rows.requires: Use as verifier and as tool: LexNLP can serve as a deterministic reference extractor for grading agent extractions (dates/amounts/durations), and its output schema defines what a world's contract-abstraction tasks should ask for (fits BigLaw-Bench SPA deal-point shape already in inventory).
rows.proof: Structured field extraction from contracts is hosted with exact answer keys: spa-deal-extraction (task_225–task_231 (7 tasks)) and maud-deal-points (task_215–task_224 (10 tasks)) pin prices, escrows, caps, fees, governing law.

rows.name: Court-deadline computation rules engines (CalendarRules / DocketCalendar / Aderant Milana / courtdeadlinecalculator.org)
rows.families: deadline chain computation from trigger events; holiday/weekend rollover handling; service-method adjustments; rule-change recalculation (amended orders)
rows.requires: The single best deterministic task family for a law-firm world: tables for court rules (rule id, trigger, offset days, day-type, rollover policy), holiday calendars per jurisdiction, service events, and a firm calendar; gold answers are exactly computable dates. No open-source engine exists, so the world must implement its own small rules engine — cheap, and grading is pure date equality. Boundary cases (holiday clusters, backward-counted deadlines) give natural flaky-task boundaries.
rows.proof: Hosted by the deadline-computation pack (task_174–task_179 (6 tasks)): rules-engine-style chained deadline computation with pinned dates and rollover/adjustment traps.

rows.name: eyecite (Free Law Project)
rows.families: citation extraction; short-form/id resolution to antecedents; brief cite-checking (validity + format); hallucinated-citation detection
rows.requires: World needs a briefs/memos document store, a citation reference table (valid reporter/volume/page tuples derived from the world's case corpus), and eyecite itself as the deterministic verifier: agent-flagged bad citations diffed against seeded errors. Ideal boundary-provable flaky-task material (seed N bad cites, require exactly those N found).
rows.proof: Hallucinated-citation detection hosted as abstention traps (phantom-citation the phantom-citation trap in task_194–task_200 (7 tasks)). Citation extraction/short-form resolution over real reporters is not (no citation corpus).

rows.name: FreeEed (shmsoft/FreeEed)
rows.families: processing pipeline operation; keyword-search culling; review-set assembly; production export
rows.requires: Defines the tool surface a world should expose: staging area for raw evidence, processing job queue with parameters (dedupe on/off, OCR, date filters), full-text search endpoint, tag/production-set tables. Task shape: 'process custodian X, apply search terms from the ESI protocol, produce set PROD001'; grade on exact doc-id membership of the production set.
rows.proof: E-discovery processing software mechanics (hashing, load files) at corpus scale.

rows.name: LRAGE (Legal RAG Evaluation toolkit)
rows.families: RAG pipeline evaluation harness; agent evaluation harness
rows.requires: Reusable infrastructure: the firm world can mount its own document corpus and task set into LRAGE to get retrieval-ablated scoring (same task with/without gold retrieval) for free — useful for boundary-proving whether a flaky task fails on retrieval or reasoning.
rows.proof: An evaluation harness, not a task set — out of scope.

rows.name: TAR Evaluation Toolkit / BMI (Cormack-Grossman Baseline Model Implementation)
rows.families: baseline comparison for review agents
rows.requires: Only needs the same oracle+corpus scaffolding as Total Recall; useful in the world as the published 'beat the baseline' bar for e-discovery tasks (agent recall@effort vs BMI recall@effort).
rows.proof: Baseline-model-implementation comparison requires corpus-scale TAR runs.
